problems.where: src/ui/physics/physicsDevices.ts stepExchange, 'withdraw' -> 'out' transition (line ~901: this.devices.loadWire("J", x.sRemoved + lead - (this.devices.skinS() - SHEATH_HUB_MM)))
problems.problem: The acceptance item 'exchange keeps the wire tip above the valve plane throughout' fails in the browser (worker mode, default start, catheter seated by seatPhysics). When the wire is reloaded on its own, its first worker frames put the J tip at or below the valve plane, and it then springs back up about 40 mm. Measured per phase (height above model.valvePlaneY): JL4 to JR4 gave pullback 62, wire 53, withdraw 30, out -2.0, in >40, and lastExchangeMinWireTipHeight = -2.05. JR4 to JL4 traced 'out t=337.37 h=40.0 | out t=337.41 h=-2.3 | out t=337.42 h=2.6 | in t=340.41 h=42.3', with lastExchangeMinWireTipHeight = -2.34. The J wire appears to be laid straight along the route, so its distal curve briefly reaches about 40 mm deeper than where the curled tip was. The unit test passes only because it starts with start.tipBackMm 60 and the plain engageScript.
problems.fix: Place the reloaded wire by where its tip actually was, not by the catheter tip plus the lead. Before removeWire(), take sWire = f.wire ? this.devices.arclength(f.wire.tip) : x.sRemoved + lead. Subtract the J curve's straightened length (a named MODEL PARAMETER), then clamp so the straight tip lies at least EXCHANGE.clearMm above the valve: loadWire('J', min(sWire - J_STRAIGHT_MM, this.devices.arclength at valve + clearMm) - (skinS - SHEATH_HUB_MM)). Alternatively, load the wire with its curve preformed. Then extend physicsDevices.test.ts so the exchange test also runs from the default start (no tipBackMm override) after engageScript plus settleThenEaseBack, the browser seat, and asserts minWire > 0 on every frame of the 'out' phase.

Alternatively, collect the bench's own costs from each new frame inside the loop. Also throw, or return a clear note, when frames === 0 instead of returning null statistics.

fix2.notes:
Applied 4 of the 5 findings; finding 5 is out of scope. All 18 package tests pass, the typecheck is clean, and I checked both exchange directions and the bench in the app.

1. Major, exchange wire reload (src/ui/physics/physicsDevices.ts, stepExchange, withdraw to out). Confirmed: the old reload put the J tip at the catheter tip plus wireLeadMm. That lead is measured along a wire that does not follow the route's centre line, so the wire went in too deep. The reload now works from where the wire tip actually was: sWire = devices.arclength(f.wire.tip), less J_STRAIGHT_MM. J_STRAIGHT_MM is the length of the J wire's curve as already defined in the solver (catheterShapes WIRE_DEFS J, 3π mm), so it is not a new MODEL PARAMETER. The tip is also capped at the deepest route arclength still EXCHANGE.clearMm above the valve, found by a new RodPhysicsDevices.deepestArclengthAbove(y) that searches along the route via LumenSet.routePoint. The finding wrote the cap as "+ clearMm"; that would put the tip deeper, so I used the cap the finding describes (the deepest point still clearMm above the valve). ROUTE_SEARCH_BEYOND_MM = 80 is only a search limit. New test in physicsDevices.test.ts: default start (no tipBackMm), the browser seat via seatPhysics, then every 'out' frame after the reload must be above the valve, with more than 30 such frames.

2. Major, cost bench (physicsDevices.ts and src/ui/sim/labSession.ts benchPhysics). Confirmed. Added a running counter, DiagnosticPhysics.costsTotal. benchPhysics now takes the last (costsTotal - fromTotal) entries, and throws a clear error when a run saw no frames or more than COST_KEEP frames. New test: "the cost record".

3. Minor, scenario brief. Confirmed in the app: the default start is in the arch. I changed the brief to "The left catheter is in the aortic arch over the J wire." I did not add a per-scenario start, because DiagScenario has no start field and adding one would mean editing types outside this package.

4. Minor, danger flag (src/physics/legacyBridge.ts legacyEngagement). Confirmed. I took the finding's third option in a slightly stronger form: isDangerous is now inLV, deep or in the conus, the same as the analytic engagement in src/simulation/engagement.ts, and dampingRisk no longer counts. Damping is still shown, through the tip trace that tipFromPhysics drives, so the colour and the trace now come from the same quantity. New test: "the danger flag".

Problem found while testing, not fixed: in Node (in-thread, config {}), the seat from the default start does not seat (it ends deep-lm or near-lm). The 90 mm pullback then barely lifts the catheter tip, because the grip slips against the deep seat and EXCHANGE.clearMaxMm ends the phase. The pinned wire then drops to about -3.4 mm during the withdraw phase. In the browser (worker, "auto" configuration) the pullback cleared and withdraw stayed at 23 to 26 mm, so this happens only from a failed deep seat. For that reason the new test checks only the 'out' phase, as the finding asked, not every frame. A real fix would make the pullback check that the tip has actually cleared (count the hand's movement that took effect, or keep pulling while the tip is still low), or have the operator pull the wire back during the withdrawal; that needs a decision from the build lead.
